--- title: "Simulation" subtitle: "Generate clean BOLD responses, noise, and matrix time series." jupyter: python3 execute: freeze: auto --- ## Simulate condition signals `simulate_bold_signal()` creates condition-wise HRF-convolved responses. The first column of `mat` is time; the remaining columns are condition signals. ::: {#d5c53e64 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} import numpy as np import pandas as pd import matplotlib.pyplot as plt import fmrimod as fm sim = fm.simulate_bold_signal( ncond=3, amps=[1.0, 1.5, 2.0], tr=2.0, seed=10, ) signals = pd.DataFrame( sim["mat"], columns=["time", "cond_1", "cond_2", "cond_3"], ) signals.head() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}
time cond_1 cond_2 cond_3
0 0.0 0.0 0.0 0.000000
1 2.0 0.0 0.0 0.000000
2 4.0 0.0 0.0 0.000017
3 6.0 0.0 0.0 0.082764
4 8.0 0.0 0.0 0.316860
``` ::: ::: ::: {#d2fb9eb5 .cell fig-height='3.5' fig-width='7' execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} ax = signals.plot(x="time", y=["cond_1", "cond_2", "cond_3"]) ax.set_xlabel("Time (s)") ax.set_ylabel("Response") plt.show() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![Three simulated condition responses with amplitudes 1.0, 1.5, and 2.0. Shared event timing makes the requested amplitude differences directly visible.](simulation_files/figure-html/cell-4-output-1.png){fig-alt=' Line chart of three simulated BOLD condition signals with the same timing and progressively larger response amplitudes.'} ::: ::: ## Add noise components `simulate_noise_vector()` combines temporal correlation, low-frequency drift, and optional physiological sinusoids. ::: {#0ed5bdf9 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} n_timepoints = 200 tr = 2.0 time = np.arange(n_timepoints) * tr whiteish = fm.simulate_noise_vector( n_timepoints, tr=tr, ar=[], ma=[], drift_amplitude=0.0, physio=False, seed=1, ) structured = fm.simulate_noise_vector(n_timepoints, tr=tr, seed=1) pd.DataFrame({ "whiteish_sd": [whiteish.std()], "structured_sd": [structured.std()], }).round(3) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ```{=html}
whiteish_sd structured_sd
0 0.924 1.708
``` ::: ::: ::: {#f6ec6c28 .cell fig-height='3.5' fig-width='7' execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} noise_df = pd.DataFrame({ "time": time, "whiteish": whiteish, "structured": structured, }) ax = noise_df.plot(x="time", y=["whiteish", "structured"], alpha=0.85) ax.set_xlabel("Time (s)") ax.set_ylabel("Noise") plt.show() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![White-noise and structured-noise simulations generated with the same seed. The structured series adds temporal dependence, drift, and physiological components.](simulation_files/figure-html/cell-6-output-1.png){fig-alt=' Two time-series lines over four hundred seconds; structured noise changes more smoothly than the white-noise comparison.'} ::: ::: ## Combine signal and noise `simulate_simple_dataset()` returns clean and noisy matrices for small method checks. ::: {#9e96c26b .cell execution_count=6} ``` {.python .cell-code} dataset = fm.simulate_simple_dataset(ncond=3, tr=2.0, snr=0.5, seed=2) dataset["clean"].shape, dataset["noisy"].shape ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=6} ``` ((157, 4), (157, 4)) ``` ::: ::: ## Simulate matrix time series `simulate_fmri_matrix()` varies event amplitude and duration across columns, mirroring the R vignette's column-specific simulation examples. ::: {#1ae716d6 .cell execution_count=7} ``` {.python .cell-code} matrix_sim = fm.simulate_fmri_matrix( n=5, total_time=120, TR=2.0, n_events=8, durations=0.5, amplitude_sd=0.2, duration_sd=0.1, noise_type="ar1", random_seed=3, ) ts = matrix_sim["time_series"].get_all_data() ts.shape, matrix_sim["ampmat"].shape, matrix_sim["durmat"].shape ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=7} ``` ((60, 5), (8, 5), (8, 5)) ``` ::: ::: ## Next - [Benchmark datasets](benchmark-datasets.qmd) - [Linear model](linear-model.qmd)
